note_tweet.text:
OpenAI Dots won a six-agent bake-off. It also costs $100 a month.

A Wired reporter ran Meta Muse, OpenAI Dots, Instinct, Anthropic Claude Duet, Google Gemini Spark, and xAI Grok Bot through five tasks. Dots scored 5/5 on lunch and the calendar-email clash. Muse took the China itinerary. Gemini Spark wrote the best headline, then 1/5 on lunch. Instinct was "most annoying."

Dots sits inside ChatGPT at $100. Muse is free and a close second. Claude Duet, a $20 wait-listed preview, had the cleanest app. Grok Bot is $30, Gemini Spark $20. Agents follow through more than last year, but they still miss an obvious overlap unless you pay up or stay on free Muse.

The best one in this test is the one most people will not buy.

#AIAgents #OpenAI #Meta

note_tweet.text:
An AI agent picked a tool for me and I paid $300 without comparing anything.

I asked my Grokbot which connector to use. It picked one. $100 got you $5 off, $300 got you $30 off. I put in $300 on the spot.

Same on Meta Muse: "Which newsletter platform should I use? Just choose one for me." Answer: Beehiiv. Done deliberating.

That's the new buyer journey. Ask the agent, the agent picks, you buy.

New surfaces just this fall: Claude Duet, Meta Muse, Instinct, Grokbot, OpenAI Dots.

How do you get recommended? More AEO, more SEO. The fundamentals didn't change. Where the decision happens did.

Neil's point: most businesses have no idea how much revenue they're losing by not optimizing for this.

My prediction: the agent recommends a plumber, then messages the plumber, "We got you this customer. Want more?" Ads come next.

Test it today: ask 3 assistants the question your buyer asks. If they don't name you, that's your roadmap.
